new comment: a shape (the game's class Shape, vtable 0x4aa250; shapes_skeletons.c: its 0x34-byte file header, then its box): a map object's model, an object list's entries, the ground layers' models ...
an actor: a mech in play, a player's or a bot's (Stage.actors, 100 slots; Scene.players = the first 16, one per player); its player record is PlayerRecord (player)
an arena as the lobby server lists it (g_serverList, 256; g_arenaPacket: the hosted arena's own, sent when it is set up; g_arenaInfoPacket / g_lobbyLeavePacket: its updates)

a game hosted from the game room, as the game server lists it (g_roomList, 256; g_roomPacket: the hosted game's own, g_roomInfoPacket / g_roomLeavePacket its updates): an ArenaRecord with the host's name
a shape manager (the game's class ShapeManager; shapes_skeletons.c; a skeleton manager is its first 0x130 bytes: SkelManager): shapes loaded by name into one block, found through a name tree
a triangle of the collision space (Space.planes; collisionTri_setup): its corners, edges, face and edge planes, unit and part; a bullet's hit (Bullet.hit)

the stage: the scene's own object at Scene + 0x1f36c8 (STAGE()), "this" of the stage_* thiscalls (the game's class Stage): the map, its objects, items, actors, particles, bullets, lights, ground, sky and collision space

the scene: the game object (the game's class Console, not its class "Scene", which is ScenePath), built once at start-up (app_startupLoad: Console_ctor, at g_scene) and holding a session's state: a match, the ARM CENTER's preview or the replays
an RGBA colour, four floats (Color4_set / set_colour_bits; g_textColour, g_textColours ...)

classes.c: the game's C++ classes as the compiler built them: constructors (set the vtable, clear the members), destructors (the vtable set back, an owned buffer freed), the "deleting" destructors and member clears; the game object built (Console_ctor, ResourceSet_ctor) and a session started (scene_startSession); the BMP reader (BMPRGBFile: image_*) and the players' flags (playerRecord_loadFlag, flag_uploadAtlas); and one-line getters, setters and vector initialisers. Most return what the original leaves in eax (usually 0 or the object).

loading.c: loading: the start-up load (app_startupLoad) and the menus' textures (menu_loadTextures); a match's load, one step per frame (game_processLoadingMode: the stages, a network client kept alive meanwhile); and the loading screen between the menus and a match: a scrolling textured cylinder (Iftex/Cylinder) behind the status text lines, faded in from black and out to black (no progress bar).

main_loop.c: one frame of the game. WinMain's message loop calls app_frame whenever no window message is waiting; it runs either a match frame (by the match's state: playing, the mech test mode, the replay viewer) or the front end's menus.

destructors.c: C++ object plumbing the compiler made for the game's classes: the "deleting" destructors (the ones in the vtables: the plain destructor run, the object freed when bit 0 of flags is set) and plain destructors of the view volume and the game object, the array constructor (crt_vectorConstructorIterator), and a view volume's matrices captured (ViewVolume_captureMatrices).

resets.c: state put back to its start: the key latches and the second key table, the server settings, the replay selection list; and two small handlers: a click closing the message box, the rank reply taken (account_takeRank).

win32.c: the game's Win32 side: the program (game_WinMain, app_init) and its window procedures, the GL window and the display mode, the text fields' hidden EDIT control, message boxes, the ending movie's MCI device and the current directory.
hud_messages.c: the HUD's centred texts (press fire, the watched player's name, the restart countdown), the help screen, and a rectangle's outline in screen pixels.

collision_tris.c: the collision space's triangles. A triangle record (CollisionTri, 0xac bytes) holds its flags, its three corners (+4), its three edges normalised (edges), its face plane (normal normal, distance dist), three edge planes (edgePlanes, 16 bytes each: the normal pointing inwards, the distance), its collision unit, its shape part, its corners' vertex indices and its unit-list links. The arithmetic is the original's: extended precision, rounded where it stores a float, and float operands taken straight from memory (fld_m / fmul_m, so a signalling NaN behaves as there).

files.c: the game's file reads and writes: the scrambled data files' record blocks (file_readScrambled / file_writeScrambled), axis.cfg (cfg_*), the pilot profiles' files (profile_*), axis.mis (mission_*), the message, character, map-info and skirmish data files (data_load*), the component catalogue, the chat macros (Chat.scp), the archives' item files, the replay file opened and closed, the launcher's files and the command line.

lists.c: list links: the free lists of the collision space's pools (a freed node or block pushed on the front of the doubly linked free list, the pool's count of nodes in use going down), and a ring appended to the menu tunnel's chain (tunnel_appendRing).

map_info.c: a map's files read: the mission file's way points and triggers, the object, play, actor and ground files, and the item file; a section is a count and that many records, each record linked to its run in a shared table (the runs follow each other; the total must match the table's own count, else a fatal message).

textures.c: the texture banks (the game's class Texture) and their manager: set up, a texture looked up and loaded by name (PTX or BMP), uploaded and bound through the GL texture cache; and the archives' name lookups (sorted 0x44-byte index entries) and file names.

shapes_skeletons.c: shapes and skeletons: their files read (binary, 3ds Max ASE, Wavefront OBJ), their managers (items loaded by name into one block, a name tree), a bone's matrix at a time, and object lists loaded and posed. A record's data is one block (allocated, or the caller's memory when it is big enough, else a fatal message).

collision_space.c: the collision space (the game's class CollisionVolume): its pools of triangles, nodes, units and blocks (a count, an array of records and a free list; emptying clears every record and links them both ways), the octree built from the map objects' triangles, and the sphere and segment tests against it.

actor_slots.c: the stage's actor slots: set up and spawned (parts, weapon, starting values, spawn records), coloured, emptied and taken out, their input records and draw; the player records and a new round reset; the pools of map objects, particles and bullets emptied; the data-loss check.

frame_loops.c: the scene's per-frame passes over its slots (bullets, particles, objects, actors and triggers; each slot in use updated unless a script holds the actors) and what they run: particles spawned, set up and updated, bullets spawned, map objects added, the triggers' way-point commands, the items' frame; also the effects' shapes and the Ladder scores added.
scores.c: the players' scores reset at a match's start, and the ranking worked out (team counts, order).
teams.c: the match's teams (team slots in Scene.teamIds: a slot picks its name, colour and score; the top player); also the stage's dynamic lights refilled (stage_refillLights).
weapons.c: an actor's weapons (switching, picking), the damage a hit does, a bot's next path point, and the bullets (fired, flying, hitting).

map_list.c: the map list (the settings form's ADVANCED list, the arena's and the game room's): per map whether it is in the rotation and its game type (0 .. 13), edited on a working copy (g_mapChoices) and kept on OK (g_mapChoicesKept); maps 22 .. 24 can never be chosen. Also the forms' map step and the lobby player's settings saved.
armc_keys.c: the ARM CENTER's keys: its parts, weapons and colour pages and the dispatch by mode. Five keys pick a part or colour slot directly; up / down step through the six with wrap-around.

edit_fields.c: opening a text field for typing (the arena screens, the game room's forms and the match's chat line) and the typed line read back. Typing goes through a hidden EDIT control (editField_createEdit) into the shared line g_inputLine, drawn with a caret at (g_editCaretX, g_editCaretY); the menu keys wait meanwhile (g_textFieldOpen, g_menuKeyGuard). Each field starts from its current text (copied in) or empty, and raises its own "being edited" flag.

game_lists.c: the lists of games to join, the game room's (window 0x9dd4a8 .. 0x9dd4b4) and the arena lobby's (0x4db8c8 .. 0x4db8d4): the games (g_sessionList) from row g_gameListTop, the page, their boxes, keys and mouse; also the lobby's SETUP PLAYER dialog.

lobby_states.c: the arena lobby and the game room: their screens set up as they are entered (camera target and look-at points, state cleared, the map list or the ranking reset), their keys and clicks by sub-screen, the lobby's frames, hosting and announcing an arena or a room game, joining an arena, and the Ladder account's and record's handling. The lobby's three sub-screens are 0 (the player's own record), 1 (the arena list) and 2 (creating an arena).

menu_cameras.c: the front end's camera moving between its home and a screen's menu point, and the free (watching) camera of screen 9999. The menu camera is a position (g_menuEyeX) and a point it looks at (g_menuCameraLook), three floats each; the menu points are 16 bytes apart from OBJ(g_camPoints) (positions) and OBJ(g_camAims) (look-at points), the home at g_menuEyeHomeX / g_menuLookHomeX. Each frame the camera eases a share of the way (the frame's time times a rate) and snaps once close enough. The arithmetic is kept in the original's order and at x87 precision (long double).

menu_init.c: front-end tables put to their start: colours, the camera points, the arena option texts, the mission list, the network state, the button outlines, the front end's start-up; also the replay list opened (replayList_open).

menu_misc.c: small pieces of the front end: the lobby player's name, the data paths, the input line and its history, the message box, the arena list's session records, the mech kept and loaded, the title screen's and the main menu's keys and clicks, the ranking's pages, the mission list's cursor and briefing pages (screen 900) and the skirmish screen's round.

menu_states.c: the front end's screens' frames and dispatch: the intro, the main menu with its replay selection dialog, the profile, setup and game-room frames, the 3D background, the mission list's and skirmish screen's pages and keys, the panels sliding in, and the way back to the menus after a match or a lost server.

profile_misc.c: pieces of the pilot profile screen (210): its pages and clicks, profiles made, named and deleted, the stat bars and the pilot grid, the save files' byte scrambling and the name checks.

room_clicks.c: the game room's handlers: its pages' clicks and keys, the Ladder login and new-ID forms checked and sent, the account change, the hosting step and the join's answer, the map previews (the room's and the arena's), the update notices, the join passwords, the white fade; also the mission list's clicks.

room_dialogs.c: the game room's dialogs and pages: opened (each a box, its fields cleared, g_roomState set to it), updated and drawn, their keys and clicks by state; joining a listed game (the room's or the arena's) and the list refreshed.

screen_enter.c: the front end's screens set up as they are entered (the main menu, the arena lobby, the setup screen, the game room, the mission list, the skirmish screen, the pilot screen, the match): each lays out its panels, sets its colours, points the menu camera at the screen with its current place as home, and clears its state; also the menus' mouse dispatch (menu_processMouse).

setup_pages.c: the setup screen's pages and menu drawn, the screens' tunnels (setup, skirmish, mission list, ARM CENTER, game room, arena lobby) and the menus of the main menu, the arena lobby's top page and the game room.

network.c: the game's network code: the TCP connections to the lobby and game servers (connect, send a request, read its reply, the lists received), DirectPlay (started, sessions hosted, joined and enumerated, messages sent and handled), the session table (200 SessionSlots at g_sessionTable) and the sixteen player slots (g_netSlots), the ping thread, this machine's address, and the match's game packets taken in (net_processGamePacket).

factors.c: the light factor pools' records built and added (factor_addFactorBy: a 0x2c-byte record of which only the kind, the colour and the kind's own fields are set; the rest is left as the stack holds it, as the originals leave it); a ground layer's lighting; a view volume sized (ViewVolume_initBy).

object_list.c: an object list: shapes placed by their own matrices, each with a buffer of shading colours, lit by light factors (shape_shadingColours, through the inverse of the shape's matrix) and a tint colour (shape_addColour), its textures bound, handed to the view volume; also the ground's layer models built (ground_buildLayerModels).

objects.c: the stage's map objects (animated scenery), actors and particles handed to the view volume, once per pass (each list walked up to its count, read again after every entry); also a map object's frame (mapObject_frame) and the frame's camera (stage_setupView).
shading.c: vertex colours lit by the light factors: a shape part's, a ground layer's; and the ground's drawing lists for the frame.

view_volume.c: the view volume: things added to its lists (an object's two points, a triangle, a quad, a camera-facing quad, a whole model), and the lists drawn; points are transformed by its matrices (columns) into clip space in the original's order; with flag 1 an entry is dropped again when all its points are outside the same clip plane; a full list sets its overflow flag.
hud_message_box.c: the message box at the top of the screen (matches and replays): one waiting message of up to four lines, or else the last events, fading out with scene->msgFade.

glyph_cells.c: the font atlases' cell tables (for each glyph its texture coordinates; every value a texel number times 1/256), the pen font (the HUD's small text) loaded and drawn, and the HUD's digits.

text_passes.c: drawing a line of text one font texture at a time: the ASCII passes (5, 8, 16, 32 pixels) and the Korean passes (lead glyphs, vowel and tail glyphs, at 13 and 31 units), colour and format codes read on the way; and what a line is made of: a Johab syllable split into its glyph rows, EUC-KR to Johab, the printable width.

text_draw.c: drawing a string in one of the four bitmap fonts, plain, centred or centred in lines. A string is drawn in up to three passes (text_passes.c), one per font texture: the Hangul initial consonants, the Hangul vowels and finals, and ASCII; each pass draws only its own characters. Colour codes "$[c]" inside a string take no room. The ASCII pass is a call the patch DLL wraps (nearest-texel sampling), so it is made through the original call site (PATCHED_CALL).
